```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 4.5,
  fig.height = 3,
  dpi = 120
)
# size each plot chunk from the plot itself (ggtargets::dag_size()), so
# nodes, lines and text look the same in every figure
knitr::opts_hooks$set(dag_fig = function(options) {
  code <- paste(options$code, collapse = "\n")
  if (!isTRUE(options$eval) || !grepl("ggplot_dag|tar_ggplot", code)) {
    return(options)
  }
  seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", globalenv())) {
    get(".Random.seed", globalenv())
  }
  wd <- getwd()
  on.exit({
    setwd(wd)
    if (is.null(seed)) {
      suppressWarnings(rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
    } else {
      assign(".Random.seed", seed, globalenv())
    }
  })
  root <- knitr::opts_knit$get("root.dir")
  if (!is.null(root)) {
    setwd(root)
  }
  size <- tryCatch(
    {
      p <- eval(parse(text = code), new.env(parent = knitr::knit_global()))
      if (ggplot2::is_ggplot(p) && !inherits(p, "patchwork")) {
        ggtargets::dag_size(p)
      }
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(size)) {
    options$fig.width <- size[["width"]]
    options$fig.height <- size[["height"]]
  }
  options
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dag_fig = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggtargets)
```

`tar_ggplot()` is the one-call entry point for a live `targets` pipeline, but everything downstream of `as_dag()` works for any directed acyclic graph.

## An edge-list data frame

The simplest input is a data frame with `from` and `to` columns - the node list is derived from the edges themselves, in the order they first appear:

```{r}
#| label: edges-only
#| fig-alt: "A small graph built from an edge-list data frame with no node table."
edges <- data.frame(from = c("a", "a", "b"), to = c("b", "c", "c"))
dag <- as_dag(edges)
ggplot_dag(dag)
```

## An edge-list data frame with a node table

Pass `nodes` to add attributes - a `label` distinct from `name`, or any column to color by (`node_color`) or to shape by (`node_shape`, see the [Customizing](customizing.html#node-shapes) article):

```{r}
#| label: edges-and-nodes
#| fig-alt: "The same graph, nodes colored by a type column from the node table."
nodes <- data.frame(
  name = c("a", "b", "c"),
  type = c("input", "process", "process")
)
dag2 <- as_dag(edges, nodes = nodes)
ggplot_dag(dag2, node_color = "type")
```

## A `tar_network()`-shaped list

`as_dag()` also accepts the list `targets::tar_network()` returns directly (`tar_dag()` is a thin wrapper around exactly this) - useful for a network object saved from another project, without needing that project's `_targets.R` or store on hand:

```{r}
#| label: tar-network-list
#| fig-alt: "A graph built directly from a tar_network()-shaped list (vertices and edges elements), the same shape targets::tar_network() returns."
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("targets", quietly = TRUE)
# saved <- targets::tar_network() # from inside the other project, once
saved <- list(
  vertices = data.frame(
    name = c("a", "b", "c"),
    type = c("stem", "stem", "stem")
  ),
  edges = data.frame(from = c("a", "b"), to = c("b", "c"))
)
ggplot_dag(as_dag(saved))
```

The `type` column of such a list is what draws a node as a circle (a regular target), a square (dynamic branches) or a triangle (an imported function or object), see `targets_node_shapes()`; the example above has only regular targets, so it has only circles and no shape legend.

## A pipeline in another folder

For a *live* pipeline elsewhere (rather than a previously saved network object), use `withr::with_dir()` (see the [Get started](ggtargets.html#plotting-a-pipeline-in-another-folder) article for the full walkthrough, including why `script`/`store` alone aren't enough):

```{r}
#| label: elsewhere
#| fig-alt: "A two-target pipeline living in a temporary project folder, plotted via withr::with_dir() from outside that folder."
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("targets", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("withr", quietly = TRUE)
project_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
withr::with_dir(project_dir, {
  targets::tar_script(
    list(targets::tar_target(x, 1), targets::tar_target(y, x + 1))
  )
})
withr::with_dir(project_dir, tar_ggplot())
```

## Converting other graph formats

ggtargets reads edge-list data frames and `tar_network()`-shaped lists; it doesn't have a method for igraph objects, Graphviz DOT files, or other graph classes directly (`as_dag()` gives a clear error naming the class). Convert to an edge-list data frame first - for igraph, `igraph::as_data_frame()` does exactly that:

```{r}
#| label: igraph
#| fig-alt: "A small graph, converted from an igraph object to an edge-list data frame."
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)
g <- igraph::graph_from_edgelist(
  matrix(c("a", "b", "a", "c", "b", "c"), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
)
edges_from_igraph <- igraph::as_data_frame(g, what = "edges")
ggplot_dag(as_dag(edges_from_igraph))
```
